subject.title: feat(cron): per-job dynamic cadence (pacing + clamped next_check)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt per-job agent-driven cron pacing as the approved first stage of the still-open automation-unification direction, including its new CLI, tool, Gateway, and persisted-job contract?
rationale: The branch is additive but establishes a durable cross-surface scheduling API; implementation review alone cannot determine whether this is the intended permanent product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor stage one
options.body: Approve the bounded pacing contract, then require upgrade and real-runtime evidence before merging this implementation.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Keep the capability but reduce or defer selected public surfaces until the umbrella design specifies the permanent cron API.

options.title: Defer with the umbrella work
options.body: Pause this PR until the broader cron/heartbeat unification proposal has an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Sponsor stage one
recommendation.body: Approve the bounded pacing contract, then require upgrade and real-runtime evidence before merging this implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked proposal and this stage-one implementation originate from the same author, making them the clearest available routing point for the intended contract.
